criteria.title: Hierarchy
criteria.instructions: Identify one primary element and up to three secondary elements using the squint and five-second checks. Equal weight, buried core insight and competing primary elements are main failures. Use only configured anchors. Missing required evidence is unknown. Never infer all checks pass from an attractive still. One penalty home per issue: hierarchy/emphasis → Hierarchy; redundant filler/message count → Information density; excess steps/fields → Flow; behavior/feedback → Interaction; category/mood → Audience; templated structure/unrelated stock styling/unclear novelty → Originality; imagery/data meaning/message clarity → Visual communication; token inconsistency → System; text size/contrast/readability → Typography; remaining usability/device adaptation → Usability. AI red flags duplicating these issues are descriptive only in Originality. Single-viewport defects never incur adaptation penalties.
anchors: Main failure described in this criterion is present.

criteria.title: Horizontal overflow
criteria.instructions: Measure document width against viewport width. This check addresses horizontal overflow only, not all spatial quality.

Reserved for a future calibrated anchor.
Reserved for a future calibrated anchor.

findings.change: Constrain oversized containers and let content wrap within the viewport.
findings.effect: Content may become readable without horizontal scrolling.

criteria.title: Typography and readability: text size
criteria.instructions: Measure visible text font sizes against the editable local threshold. This is a bounded typography check, not message clarity or a general readability certification.
anchors: Visible text falls below the configured minimum size.
Reserved for a future calibrated anchor.

criteria.title: Message clarity and redundant filler
criteria.instructions: Judge whether headings and action wording convey the task clearly. Flag redundant filler microcopy, not all microcopy. Preserve essential labels, errors, instructions and useful onboarding. Do not score font size, spacing, line height or contrast.
anchors: Vague or redundant wording materially obscures the task or next action.
Several avoidable filler phrases compete with needed information.
Mostly specific wording with limited redundant explanation.
Specific, concise task language; essential labels, errors and instructions remain.

findings.label: Replace redundant filler
findings.problem: Redundant or vague wording competes with task-specific information.
findings.change: Replace redundant filler with specific task or action wording. Preserve essential labels, errors, instructions and useful onboarding.
findings.effect: Readers may find the next action with less effort.

criteria.title: Image alternative-text presence
criteria.instructions: Check only whether img elements have an alt attribute. An empty alt may mark decoration. Presence does not establish appropriate text or accessibility compliance.
anchors: At least one sampled image lacks an alt attribute.
Reserved for a future calibrated anchor.
Reserved for a future calibrated anchor.
Every sampled image has an alt attribute; quality remains untested.

findings.label: Review image alternatives
findings.problem: A sampled image lacks an alt attribute.
findings.change: Add useful alternative text to informative images; use an empty alt only for decorative images.
findings.effect: Screen-reader context may improve after human review.

criteria.title: Apparent affordances
criteria.instructions: Judge only whether controls look actionable in this default still image. Never infer that clicking works, feedback exists, validation is correct or keyboard access works.
anchors: Primary controls do not appear actionable.
Several controls have ambiguous visual affordances.
Controls look actionable with minor ambiguity.
Controls clearly communicate their apparent role in the captured state.

findings.label: Clarify control appearance
findings.problem: A visible control has an ambiguous apparent role.
findings.change: Give the control a clear visual affordance without claiming its behavior is verified.
findings.effect: People may recognize available actions more easily.

criteria.title: Verified interaction behavior
criteria.instructions: Requires scripted interaction assertions and observed outcomes. Screenshots and DOM availability cannot establish behavior.
anchors: Verified interaction fails the core task.
Verified interaction has significant defects.
Tested behavior works with minor defects.
Tested interaction and recovery work intentionally.

criteria.title: Cross-device prioritization
criteria.instructions: Compare the supplied matched desktop/mobile captures for responsive reprioritization and navigation changes. Do not penalize clipping, small text or local spacing again: those belong to LAY/TYPE. Only identify distinct cross-device prioritization failures.
anchors: Matched captures show task-critical priority lost across devices.
Cross-device priority or navigation changes significantly hinder the task.
Sensible cross-device priority with minor tradeoffs.
Intentional reflow and reprioritization across the matched captures.

findings.label: Reprioritize content across devices
findings.problem: The matched captures show an inconsistent priority across devices.
findings.change: Adapt content priority and navigation to the mobile task without adding another fix for local overflow or type size.

criteria.title: Motion quality
criteria.instructions: Requires video or temporal evidence and a verified temporal judge. Static SubQ inputs cannot establish animation timing, smoothness, interruption behavior or quality. No video judging in this baseline.
anchors: Verified obstructive motion.
Verified distracting motion.
Verified purposeful motion with minor defects.
Verified task-appropriate motion or intentional stillness.

Overlapping issues require one scoring home; supporting checks never add deductions. AI-isms belong under Originality without an authorship claim.
Missing evidence stays unknown. No missing-evidence normalization or cross-viewport total.
